raw_response:
I am 50 years old, and I have been working this land since I was 15. My mother taught me everything I know. I never went to school, not even one day. I cannot read those papers the county people bring, and I do not trust their talk. I watch what Old Wang and Auntie Li do, and if their fields look good, I copy them. My farm is 16.9 mu, which is bigger than most around our village, so I have to be careful with money, but I also know that cutting back on inputs is a bigger risk than spending too much. A bad harvest means disaster; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. My husband and son work in Handan city and send money home, so it is mostly me and my daughter-in-law in the fields. We hire two people during cotton picking and wheat harvest.

This year I will do the same as last year. I start from what I did before and adjust only a little.

For cotton, I have 8 mu. Cotton is my cash crop. I plant hybrid Bt cotton seeds, the kind I buy from the seed shop in town. Last year I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that is 100 jin — and then I top-dressed with half a bag of urea when flowering started, and another half bag when the bolls came. I also spread about 20 jin of potassium fertilizer per mu because the dealer said cotton likes it, and I saw Old Wang do it. That is a lot of fertilizer, but cotton needs to eat. I would rather put a little too much than watch the bolls fall off. I irrigate four times from my well: after planting, at flowering, when the bolls are fattening, and once in August if the rain does not come. I spray pesticides five times because the bollworms and red spiders always come, no matter what. For cotton I plough deep, not just rotary, because the roots need to go deep into the soil. Last year I got about 300 jin of seed cotton per mu, and I expect the same this year if the weather is normal.

For wheat, I have 5 mu. I planted it last fall after rotary tilling. I used improved seeds, the same kind my neighbor used — his wheat looked thick and strong. Now at green-up time I will spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 50 jin total for the field. I irrigate three times: once now in spring, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice, once for weeds and once for disease. I expect about 900 jin per mu, which is around 450 kg.

For maize, I plant 5 mu right after we cut the wheat in June. I rotary till fast and plant hybrid maize seeds. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu goes in the holes at planting, and then half a bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. Irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is dry. Spray twice — once for weeds and once for armyworms. Last year I got 1,100 jin per mu, so I expect around 550 kg again.

For mungbean, I plant 3.9 mu on the east plot. I keep my own seeds from last year, the traditional green mungbean. Mungbean does not need much feeding. Half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu is enough. Irrigate twice, once when flowering and once when the pods are filling. Spray once for pod borers. Last year I got 180 jin per mu, so about 90 kg.

Fertilizer prices went up again. Urea is 20 yuan more per bag than last year. But I will not cut back. If I use less and lose yield, that is thousands of yuan gone. If I use the same as last year, I spend a few hundred more on fertilizer. That is easy thinking. Old Wang is doing the same amount as last year, so I will too.
